citacoes.trecho: Specifically, we present three creative strategies: XSP for improving problem comprehension, Syntax-Aware XSP (SA-XSP) for mitigating syntax errors, and Testcase-Driven Logic Error Debugging (TDLED) for resolving logic errors through test case feedback.

Our experiments on 30 LLMs, ranging from 0.5B, 70B, to 671B parameters and including 5 reasoning models, demonstrate that the proposed methods improve accuracy by up to 27.5%, especially in smaller models, with syntax error reductions of up to 60% and logic error corrections by up to 30%.
However, they often produce syntax and logic errors, which reduces their usability in production environments.
Moreover, this method often introduces new errors during the revision process, resulting in minimal overall gains and a cycle of diminishing returns.
We propose two new approaches, the Solution-Oriented Logic Error Debugging (SOLED) and the Testcase-Driven Logic Error Debugging (TDLED), to guide LLMs in correcting logic errors.

XSP mitigates these issues by clearly separating instructions, inputs/outputs, and examples into tagged sections, thereby reducing ambiguity and enhancing code-generation accuracy, particularly for smaller models with limited reasoning capacity.
While prior work has emphasized post hoc debugging, we propose a proactive approach: Syntax-Aware XML-Structured Prompts (SA-XSP), an extension of XSP.
We design three templates, each tailored to one of these common error types, to guide models toward generating syntactically correct code.
To evaluate this, we tested 30 LLMs on 3,000+ Codeforces problems, comparing unstructured prompts with the three SA-XSP variants.
For each problem, the model first generates an incorrect solution, which is then fed back to it with a prompt to revise and fix any errors.
This cycle repeats up to three times.
SOLED tests whether solution hints (English or pseudocode) help models overcome logic errors by asking them to re-generate solutions from scratch.
Fig. 12 illustrates how SOLED guides models using structured prompts that include a high-level algorithmic strategy and supporting pseudocode.
For each failed attempt, the model receives up to five structured test cases showing inputs, its incorrect outputs, and the expected outputs, encouraging it to reconcile discrepancies.
Across all sizes, TDLED plus reasoning consistently delivers the highest NI, offering a viable approach to reduce logic errors.

Our three methods - XML-Structured Prompt (XSP) for structural clarity, Syntax-Aware XSP (SA-XSP) for reducing syntax errors, and Testcase-Driven Logic Error Debugging (TDLED) for resolving logic errors via test-case feedback - are evaluated on 3,000+ Codeforces problems across 30 LLMs (0.5B–72B parameters).

extracoes.selecao_motivo: Técnica focal ainda não representada; exceção ao alvo de três. Não há tabela com XSP contra o prompt simples; a primeira figura com o contraste é a Fig. 8, sem valores legíveis, e o valor impresso só aparece em prosa como faixa de diferença.
extracoes.localizador: p. 5 (PDF e impressa), Fig. 8; p. 3, seção IV

citacoes.trecho: Evaluating 30 LLMs on Codeforces problems, we find that XSP improves performance across all model sizes (Fig. 8), with gains of 12.5–27.5% for models under 20B parameters and 7.5–10% for models over 40B.

qualidade.justificativa: Objetivo explícito (mitigar erros de sintaxe e lógica com prompts estruturados em XML) e contribuições enumeradas para XSP, SA-XSP, SOLED e TDLED.

Descreve as estratégias, as equações de % Dec., RI e NI e mostra trechos dos prompts, mas não informa o número exato de problemas, o prompt da geração inicial, a definição operacional de acurácia, parâmetros de decodificação, número de execuções, nem quais modelos entram em cada experimento além dos listados nas tabelas.

Há comparadores executados (prompt não estruturado para XSP e SA-XSP; acurácia inicial e depuração iterativa para SOLED e TDLED), mas os valores de base de XSP e as acurácias inicial e final não são impressos, e SA-XSP não é comparado com XSP.
